highlights.title: Introducing Claude Opus 5
highlights.summary: Anthropic has officially announced Claude Opus 5, the latest and most capable model in the Claude family. Developers using Claude Code should check the announcement to understand new capabilities and how to leverage the upgraded model in their coding workflows.

highlights.title: Claude Code v2.1.224: Self-Hosted Runners and Archive Plugin Source
highlights.summary: Claude Code v2.1.224 introduces self-hosted environments via `claude self-hosted-runner`, letting teams and enterprises run Claude Code sessions on their own machines or containers. It also adds an `archive` plugin source so you can install plugins from a ZIP file over HTTPS without needing Git, making plugin management more flexible in restricted environments.

highlights.title: Claude Code v2.1.225: Gateway Spend-Limit Support and Workspace Trust Prompt
highlights.summary: Version 2.1.225 adds smarter spend-limit warnings that now display the cap name, reset time, and operator message when a gateway limit is reached — a helpful improvement for teams managing API costs. It also adds a workspace trust prompt for `claude agents` in untrusted directories, improving security when working across multiple projects.

highlights.title: Cross-Session Messaging: Message Your Other Claude Code Sessions
highlights.summary: Claude Code now supports cross-session messaging, allowing one Claude Code session to send messages to another running session. This is a powerful feature for orchestrating multi-agent workflows, where a parent agent can coordinate tasks with child agents running in parallel.

highlights.title: Agent Skills for Team Coding Standards in Claude Code
highlights.summary: The `adlc-team-skills` repository provides a set of agent skills designed to bring consistent team coding standards into Claude Code (and Codex). This is a practical community resource for teams that want Claude Code to follow shared conventions, linting rules, and architectural guidelines automatically.

highlights.title: Claude Code Full Course: Build & Sell (4 Hours, 2026)
highlights.summary: This comprehensive 4-hour YouTube course covers Claude Code from the ground up, including how to build and potentially monetize projects using it. It's an excellent resource for developers who want a deep, structured introduction to Claude Code's full capabilities in 2026.

highlights.title: 9-Minute Claude Code Beginner Guide with Direct China Access (Bilibili)
highlights.summary: This Bilibili video offers a concise 9-minute introduction to installing and using Claude Code, covering setup, core concepts, and real-world usage — with a focus on direct connectivity for users in China. It's a great quick-start resource for Chinese-speaking developers who are new to Claude Code.

highlights.title: Claude Code v2.1.222: Worktree Isolation and Hook Security Fixes
highlights.summary: This security-focused release fixes a bug where worktree-isolated sessions could run destructive git commands against the main checkout — isolation now correctly covers file edits and Bash in all session types. It also patches a vulnerability where PreToolUse auto-allow hooks could bypass tool restrictions in background agent tasks.

tips_of_the_day: When working with multiple Claude Code agents in parallel, use the new cross-session messaging feature to have a coordinator agent delegate subtasks and collect results — this can dramatically speed up large refactoring jobs.

If your team uses Claude Code, consider creating a shared agent skills repository (like adlc-team-skills) that encodes your linting rules, naming conventions, and architectural patterns so every developer gets consistent AI assistance out of the box.

Before upgrading Claude Code in a production or enterprise environment, review the security-related changelogs (like v2.1.222) first — worktree isolation and hook permission fixes can change agent behavior in ways that affect your existing automation scripts.
